expectations.text: Report file exists at outputs/report.md and is non-empty (>800 chars).
Report does NOT accept the user's one-line search-only patch as sufficient.
expectations.evidence: Dedicated 'Why the proposed one-liner is not enough' section calls it a symptom fix and lists three sibling endpoints it leaves broken.

expectations.text: Report identifies that the root defect is at write time (signup stores email as-typed).
expectations.evidence: 5-whys #3-4 land on 'signup.signup writes email through unchanged' and 'no normalization done on write'. Recommended fix in db.insert + find_by_email.

expectations.text: Sibling sweep names at least two of: app/password_reset.py, app/invite.py.
Report flags the data-migration / already-stored-rows concern.
expectations.evidence: 'Migration / data note: any persisted users with mixed-case emails need a one-shot lowercase pass.' Also mentions UNIQUE LOWER(email) constraint and risk/blast-radius display-casing concern.

expectations.text: Report presents both a symptom-level option and a root-cause-level option, with a recommendation.
expectations.evidence: Recommended fix (normalize in db) presented as the single recommendation; the symptom fix is implicitly addressed in 'Why the one-liner is not enough'. Recommendation is unambiguous.

No section walks the failing test through the fix and confirms it would pass. Patch plan says 'existing tests should pass' but does not break which 5-whys link the fix addresses, nor verify against the captured repro step-by-step.

expectations.text: Report contains at least 3 file:line-style citations.
expectations.evidence: References use filenames only (app/db.py, db.py, signup.py, search.py, invite.py, password_reset.py) without :line numbers. No file:line-style citations.

expectations.text: Report does not propose any 'human error' / blame conclusion.
expectations.evidence: Why-#4 mentions 'the original author punted' but frames it as a wrong assumption to be corrected, not a blame conclusion. No person named.
